description.narrative: Oxfam in partnership with PARC will address the acute Water, Hygiene and Sanitation (WASH) needs. Prevention is Oxfam’s main courseof action for public health risks and Result 2 seeks to reduce the effect of poor WASH and IPC infrastructure that leadsto health acquired infections, transmission of diseases within the target communities, health facilities, education, and public feeding centres. The action will contribute to providing critical WASH needs of the vulnerable conflict-affected returnees, host and IDPs households in Gaza and Gaza North Governorates. Oxfam will implement this action in partnership with PARC in close coordination with PWA and CMWU. This action will address the critical need for access to safe and inclusive WASH services in conflict affected areas, particularly for IDPs in makeshift camps, IDPs in less served formal shelters and most vulnerable communities in hard-to-reach areas. The project will include performing quick fixes to repair damaged water sources and distribution systems to restore essential access to safe drinking water, while the installation of water storage tanks with taps will enhance water accessibility at these sites. Furthermore, the repair and construction of WASH facilities at public health, educational, and feeding centres will create safer environments for community gatherings and services. Special attention to shared latrines for women-headed families underscores the commitment to gender-sensitive approaches in humanitarian responses. Hygiene promotion campaigns and the provision of infection prevention and control (IPC) supplies, hygiene kits and WASH non-food items are critical in mitigating outbreaks and promoting good hygiene practices. Lastly, the safe collection and transfer of solid waste will help maintain sanitary conditions, reducing the risk of disease transmission in overcrowded settings. Collectively, these initiatives not only aim to meet immediate needs but also promote long-term health and safety for affected communities. WASH proposed response will focus on the following main approaches First, Oxfam will guarantee access to quality water supply to the affected population through various activities (water trucking, desalination unit, quick fixes on existing infrastructure –water supply and wastewater pipelines) depending on the typology of the location and its population. Second, Oxfam and PARC will also focus on access to safe and dignified sanitation facilities through repair of disaggregated communal latrines at IDP sites and construction of self-built shared household latrines for returnees and IDPs at makeshift sites, following sanitation working group guidelines. All repaired and installed latrines will include cleaning kits, with a focus on accessibility and safety for women, people with special needs, and providing specific tools for PWDs and the elderly. In response to public health risks, Oxfam and PARC, in collaboration with CMWU, will support mechanical and manual desludging of household latrine pits at the returnees and IDP sites. In parallel of these two approaches Oxfam and its partner will raise awareness among communities around hygiene and solid waste collection. Oxfam and its partner will distribute emergency HKs and WASH NFI including family hygiene kits, MHM kits, commodes and bedpans for most vulnerable individuals and people with special needs. Finally, Oxfam and its partner will provide IPC and WASH support to health facilities, education centres and feeding centres with consideration thatintegrated approach ofIPC and WASH where IPC cannot be met without WASH services, the later providing the basis for adequate IPC (water, sanitation and hygiene services). The response will contribute to limit human-to-human transmission, including reducing secondary infections among close contacts and healthcare workers and strengthening health facilities.

participating-org.narrative: In 1983 a small group of agronomists founded the Palestinian Agricultural Relief Committees (PARC), which has since developed into one of the most important Palestinian non-governmental organisations providing services to poor and marginalised farmers onthe West Bank and Gaza Strip, working to make agricultural businesses grow. PARC#s goal is to promote an economic and social climate that would allow the Palestinian agricultural sector to develop sustainably. Another goal is to improve the living standard of Palestinians living in rural areas, especially of poor farming families. PARC provides a broad range of agricultural extension services. It is active in land reclamation and in building rural access roads. The organisation advocates the improvementof rural women#s economic position. It is part of an Oxfam Novib-funded three-year gender-focus program. In 1991 PARC got an ISO-certification. It was the first and so far only non-governmental organisation in the Arab world to obtain one. It has also developed an impressive strategic ten-year plan for the 1998-2008 period. Together with several other agricultural non-governmental organisations (NGOs) PARC has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Ministry of Agriculture, which sees PARC#s workasindependent and complementary to its own. PARC is active in a network of Palestinian NGOs and a member of the governing committee of the Palestinian NGO-network. Oxfam Novib has been supporting PARC since 1982. In 1999 Oxfam Novib, ICCO, Christian Aid (UK) and Oxfam Great Britain set up a donor consortium to support PARC. This provides PARC a measure of long-term financial security. It also makes technical and organisational assistance available to PARC in further developing its program.
